key: “These men,” replied Confucius, “travel beyond the rule of life. I travel within it.
s: Hearing from Tzŭ Kung of friends singing over a corpse, Confucius answers; Guo Xiang, on chapter 6, reads outside and inside as one, the sage roaming outside to enlarge the inside, a roaming the text gives these friends lest readers refuse it in Confucius.
src: Guo Xiang, Zhuangzi zhu, chapter 6, zh.wikisource (Nanhua zhenjing zhushu, juan 8, Zhengtong Daozang), revision 6354439 (2026)

opened.edition: zh.wikisource 南華真經註疏 卷八 (Zhengtong Daozang, DZ0745), revision 6354439, Guo Xiang's 注 only
opened.locator: 大宗師, on 孔子曰：彼，遊方之外者也；而丘，遊方之內者也 (Giles 6.145 to 6.148 run; the text line packet-labelled 6.145)

evidence.words: 夫理有至極，外內相冥…故聖人常遊外以弘內，無心以順有…若直就稱仲尼之如此，或者將據所見以排之，故超聖人之內迹，而寄方外於數子。
evidence.gloss: (On ‘they roam outside the bounds, I roam within’:) the pattern of things has its utmost point, where outside and inside merge as one. … So the sage always roams outside so as to enlarge the inside, and with no mind of his own goes along with what is. … Had it been said outright that Confucius was so, some would have rejected it on the strength of what they saw; so the text passes over the sage’s inner traces and lodges the beyond-the-bounds in these few men.

reason: Problem holds. Re-opened packet.js zhuangzi 9 --verse 6.145 (juan 8, revision 6354439; the Chinese 孔子曰：彼，遊方之外者也；而丘，遊方之內者也 is the key verse’s line by its opening words). ‘Darkly one’ replaced by ‘one’ (外內相冥), and the reason for the lodging restored: had it been said outright of Confucius, some would reject it on what they saw, so the beyond-the-bounds is lodged in these few men (若直就稱仲尼之如此，或者將據所見以排之，故…寄方外於數子). The sage roaming outside to enlarge the inside is 故聖人常遊外以弘內. Plain sense, key, place and src unchanged. verse.js ok (Zhuangzi 6.148, at 591); entry-check ok, 44 words.
